groups.title: Cold Relief Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve the symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 1 tablet 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cold symptoms: sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, aches
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; regular alcohol use

groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Cold Relief Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 capsules per dose; for people aged 8 years to under 15 years, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cold symptoms: runny nose, congestion, sneezing, sore throat, fever, aches
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 8 years; regular alcohol use

groups.title: Bile Secretion Support Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as supportive treatment for liver disease caused by insufficient bile secretion and for biliary tract (bile duct, gallbladder) disease, and for chronic conditions related to it.
groups.usage: For adults, 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet 3 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, or have severe biliary obstruction, fulminant hepatitis or radiolucent calcified gallstones. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Supportive treatment for liver and biliary tract disease
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Severe biliary obstruction; fulminant hepatitis; calcified gallstones

groups.title: Antispasmodic Antacid Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for stomach pain, abdominal pain, colic, excess stomach acid and heartburn.
groups.usage: For adults (aged 15 years and over), 2 tablets 2 to 3 times a day; for people aged 8 years to under 15 years, 1 tablet 2 to 3 times a day, after or between meals. When taken 2 or more times a day, leave an interval of at least 4 hours.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are a child aged 7 years or under, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Stomach and abdominal pain, colic, excess acid, heartburn
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years or under; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as supportive treatment for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after trauma or surgery, and infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 capsule (300 mg) 2 to 4 times a day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, pain and swelling after trauma or surgery
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Maximum 1200 mg a day; gastrointestinal bleeding

groups.title: Laxative Enteric-coated Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for constipation and for relief of the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 1 to 2 tablets once a day at bedtime (on an empty stomach). Start with the smallest amount and increase or decrease it gradually while watching the shape and condition of the stool.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have an acute abdominal condition (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and similar), intestinal obstruction, or galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Constipation and related bloating, poor appetite and haemorrhoids
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; acute abdominal disease; bowel obstruction

groups.title: Analgesic Antipyretic Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, low back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain and sprain pain.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over or adults, 1 to 2 capsules per dose; for people aged 11 years to under 15 years, 1 capsule per dose, 1 to 3 times a day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours and avoiding an empty stomach. For people aged 8 years to under 11 years, 1 capsule per dose, 1 to 2 times a day, leaving an interval of at least 6 hours and avoiding an empty stomach.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Headache, toothache, sore throat, joint and muscle pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 8 years; at least 4 hours between doses; regular alcohol use

groups.title: Digestive Enzyme Enteric-coated Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, a feeling of heaviness, promotion of digestion, and a feeling of fullness in the stomach caused by indigestion.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over, 2 tablets 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are a child aged 7 years or under, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, stomach fullness
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years or under; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Calcium Antacid Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for the antacid action and symptom relief of gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and for calcium supplementation.
groups.usage: For gastric or duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, 2 to 10 tablets (1 to 5 g) a day in 3 to 4 divided doses; for calcium supplementation, 3 to 6 tablets (1.5 to 3 g) a day in 1 to 2 divided doses. Adjust appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution: Do not exceed a maximum of 15 tablets (7.5 g) a day. Do not take if you have severe high blood calcium or severe high urine calcium, or hyperparathyroidism. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Antacid for ulcer, gastritis and excess acid; calcium supplementation
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Maximum 15 tablets a day; high blood calcium

groups.title: Antihistamine Decongestant Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes caused by a head cold and by allergic or vasomotor rhinitis.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet per dose; for children aged 12 to 14 years, 1/2 tablet per dose, 3 times a day after each meal.
groups.caution: If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes from a cold or rhinitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Serious skin reactions

groups.title: Acetaminophen Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, period pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: For children aged 12 years and over and adults, 1 to 2 tablets 3 to 4 times a day, every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 4 g (8 tablets) a day. Take the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Fever and pain from a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 12 years; maximum 4 g a day; regular alcohol use

groups.title: Mucolytic Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as a mucolytic and expectorant in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 capsule (300 mg) 2 to 3 times a day. For acute respiratory disease, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, or have liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe renal impairment. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Mucolytic and expectorant in acute and chronic respiratory disease
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Liver cirrhosis, peptic ulcer, severe renal impairment

groups.title: Antihistamine Tablet for Skin Symptoms
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for urticaria, eczema, itching and dermatitis caused by lacquer and similar plants.
groups.usage: For adults and people aged 15 years and over, 1 tablet 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, are a child under 15 years, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Urticaria, eczema, itching, plant dermatitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; pregnancy, breastfeeding; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Expectorant Capsule

groups.usage: For acute disease, adults take 1 capsule (200 mg) 3 times a day and children aged 6 to 14 years take 1 capsule (200 mg) 2 times a day, before meals with a small amount of water. For chronic disease, adults take 1 capsule (200 mg) 2 times a day and children aged 6 to 14 years take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) 3 times a day.

groups.title: Intestinal Adsorbent Powder
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for acute and chronic enteritis, acute and chronic diarrhoea, acute dysentery, and abnormal intestinal fermentation of various causes.
groups.usage: For adults, 2 g 3 times a day, with 4 g for the first dose. For young children, 1 g 3 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or a genetic problem such as glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
